generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, looking out for learning by doing shapes how you read each module. A research methods unit, a work placement in a mental health service, or a volunteering role on a helpline are all chances to learn by doing. Each time one appears, you can name it, work out its form, and ask what it could give you.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students are offered a placement in a mental health service and a lab-based research project. One signs up to both without thinking about what they are. The other names each as learning by doing, sees that one is a placement and the other a lab project, and works out the skills each could build. By the end, the second student can point to real experience with clients and with data that employers value.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, learning by doing turns up as placements, research projects, fieldwork and volunteering. When you bring the three ideas together, you can spot each chance, name its form, and see what it offers your development. That habit helps you build towards the kind of psychologist you want to be.

check.body: A student spots a live project in their course, names it as learning by doing, sees it could build real skills, and signs up. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: They brought the three ideas together as one practice: they recognised the chance, placed its form, and saw what it offered.
_items.feedback: Yes. Naming it, placing its form and seeing its benefit is the one practice at work.

_items.text: They skipped straight to signing up without knowing what the project was.
_items.feedback: They did name it as learning by doing first. That is part of the practice.

_items.text: They treated the project as ordinary classroom study.
_items.feedback: They saw it as learning by doing, which is the opposite of ordinary classroom study.

_items.text: They only looked at the benefits and ignored what the project actually was.
_items.feedback: They named it and placed its form too, not only its benefits.
